correctness.rationale: The primary source proves B=d eta-2 Phi=-2 g(phi h_a .,.) and proves that Killing xi is equivalent to h being skew-adjoint, so h_a=h. For a skew operator K, the associated two-form has squared norm one half of the Hilbert--Schmidt squared norm. Because h is horizontal and phi is orthogonal there, this yields ||B||^2=2||h||_HS^2. The source independently proves Ric(xi,xi)=2n+||h||_HS^2. Finally B is phi-anti-invariant while Phi is phi-invariant, hence orthogonal, and ||Phi||^2=n. These identities give the claimed defect norm, Reeb-form norm, and angle law with no omitted sign or normalization factors. The packaged checker replays the algebra and the five-dimensional specialization.

value.rationale: The primary source makes characteristic Ricci curvature the decisive criterion for whether a Killing quasi-contact structure is actually K-contact, while its new examples show strict structures genuinely occur. The finding upgrades that yes/no criterion to an exact quantitative measurement: Ricci excess is precisely the squared incompatibility with contact-metric geometry, and the full Reeb-form norm and compatibility angle become intrinsic curvature observables. On the source's canonical one-parameter family, the deformation parameter becomes the tangent of that angle. These are natural structural invariants of the new examples and general Killing quasi-contact class, not an arbitrary numerical slice or a mere renaming.
